bull.b: Long-term NBMs materially improve revenue visibility by linking future sales to multi-year customer commitments. Their growing share of bits and contractual financial guarantees can support planning, deepen strategic relationships, and make the business model less dependent on spot-market demand.

The shift toward datacenter storage strengthens SanDisk’s exposure to a faster-growing, strategically important end market. Rising datacenter mix can diversify the portfolio beyond consumer devices and support sustained demand as AI and infrastructure workloads expand.

Strong operating cash conversion and very low leverage provide substantial financial flexibility. This supports investment in technology and capacity, improves resilience through market cycles, and allows capital returns without relying heavily on additional borrowing.

bear.b: The sharp reversal from losses to exceptional profitability demonstrates meaningful earnings cyclicality. If memory conditions weaken, margins, cash generation, and returns could contract rapidly, making current financial performance less dependable across a full industry cycle.

Weakness in consumer markets reduces diversification while PC and smartphone demand adjusts. A delayed recovery could restrain near-term growth, leave the company more reliant on datacenter customers, and increase the impact of fluctuations in a narrower set of end markets.

The NBM model improves visibility but also concentrates revenue among fewer major customers. This can increase bargaining and execution risk if a strategic partner changes plans, delays purchases, or negotiates terms, even though financial guarantees provide some contractual protection.
